brief.headline: Nifty Surges 1.85% to 25819.25; Rupee Hits 8-Month High on $14.7B Inflows
brief.summary: Indian equities rallied strongly in the prior session as the Nifty 50 surged 1.85% to 25819.25, supported by broad gains in FMCG and banking stocks. Robust foreign inflows of $14.7 billion in November pushed the rupee to an eight-month high of 92.22 against the dollar. Meanwhile, global markets remain watchful over fresh US tariff proposals targeting Indian exports.

takeaways.text: Rupee hit an 8-month high of 92.22 as November FII inflows reached $14.7 billion, with ANZ seeing further potential gains to 90-91.
US Trade Representative proposed extra tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, which could fall to 17% under a trade deal.
Wipro secured a multi-year finance transformation deal from bp to absorb 3,000 employees across India, Hungary, and Malaysia.
Schaeffler AG plans to sell a 6% stake in Schaeffler India via a ₹3,188 crore block deal at ₹3,400 per share.
US Q3 GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, while October core PCE rose to 3.8%, strengthening Fed rate hike expectations.
S&P signaled a potential one-notch credit rating downgrade for Nvidia due to management and governance concerns.

sections.india: The Nifty 50 surged 1.85% to close at 25819.25 yesterday, led by FMCG heavyweights including HUL and Britannia. Strong foreign buying pushed November stock inflows to $14.7 billion, carrying USD/INR to an 8-month high of 92.22. However, export sectors face headline risks following the US proposal to levy additional tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, subject to ongoing trade negotiations.
sections.world: US markets ended mixed overnight as strong economic data reinforced expectations of sustained Federal Reserve tightening. US Q3 GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, while October PCE inflation accelerated to 3.8%. Asian markets opened higher today, with the Nikkei 225 rising 1.54% and Hang Seng up 2.18% following a late Wall Street recovery.
sections.tech: Nvidia faces credit rating risks as S&P Global Ratings signaled a potential one-notch downgrade over governance concerns following executive turnover. In satellite technology, the FCC approved SpaceX's initiative to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites. Meanwhile, Amazon is in discussions to permit Meta's Muse AI shopping agent on its marketplace platform.
